intro: Read the distance from a v–t graph.

widget.instructions: The graph is the sprinter's velocity against time; the area under it is the distance.

args.text: Your distance is the area of some shape under this graph: check which parts you included.

stem: A sprinter's v–t graph rises in a straight line from 0 to {{v}} m/s over {{t1}} s, then stays at {{v}} m/s for {{t2}} s.
How far does the sprinter run in this time?

hints.text: Distance is the area under a v–t graph.
Split the area into a triangle (speeding up) and a rectangle (steady speed).
Triangle: ½ × base × height; rectangle: width × height.

area-uses-final-velocity.text: You used a rectangle of height {{v}} m/s for the whole time. During the first {{t1}} s the sprinter was slower, so that part is a triangle.

area-misses-triangle.text: You left out the distance covered while speeding up: the triangle under the first part of the graph.

dimension-mismatch.text: Check the unit: the answer is a length.

generic.text: Area under the v–t graph: triangle + rectangle.

area-uses-final-velocity.back: The area under it: a sloping part makes a triangle or trapezium, not a rectangle of height v.

area-misses-triangle.front: v–t graph: acceleration phase then constant speed. Distance?

generic.back: The area under it (triangle + rectangle for this shape).

accessibility.altText: A v–t graph rising from 0 to {{v}} m/s and then flat.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: The graph is for reading; type your answer in the box.
